# Placing windows (place_windows)

`place_windows` puts one window or several at a rectangle the caller chooses, through MCP or `smbact-cli place`
([cli/README.md](../cli/README.md#placing-windows-place)). It is phase 1 of [geometry-automation-spec.md](./geometry-automation-spec.md);
`smbact://` links (phase 2) and saved scenes (phase 3) come later. The geometry is computed once, in
`app-native/shared/placement/` (pure TypeScript); the main-window renderer runs the executor against the native window
module (`McpService.place`), with the displays main sends along.

```json
{"placements": [
  {"app": "Safari", "frame": "0,0,60%,100%"},
  {"app": "Terminal", "frame": "60%,0,40%,100%"},
  {"app": "Slack", "display": "next", "anchor": "center", "width": "1200dip", "height": "800dip", "if_missing": "skip"}
]}
```

- **Where positions point.** By default `area: "work"`: the work area of the window's display (without menu bar, Dock,
  taskbar, panels), so `0,0` is its usable corner and `60%` is 60 % of its width. `area: "full"` is the whole display;
  `area: "screen"` is absolute coordinates as `list_windows` reports them (no display, anchor, grid, dip or shares
  then). `display` picks the display: `current` (the window's, default), an index, `main`, `active`, `cursor`, `next`,
  `prev`, `name:<name>`, `id:<id>` or a bare name; alone it moves the window there keeping its place and size relative
  to the work area.
- **Lengths.** An integer or `"<n>px"` is native units (the space of `list_windows`, `get_capabilities.coordinates`);
  `"<n>dip"` is scaled by the display's scale (macOS and the Wayland backends: 1); `"<p>%"` (up to 4 decimals) and
  `"<a>/<b>"` are shares of the area, floored in exact integer arithmetic; `"rel:<value>"` adds to the current frame
  (`rel:` requests are not idempotent). When `x` and `width` are both shares, the two edges are computed and the width
  is their difference, so neighbours (`0,0,60%,100%` and `60%,0,40%,100%`, or three `1/3`s) tile with no gap.
- **Anchors and grids.** `anchor` (nine points) attaches the window to a point of the area, `x` / `y` become inward
  offsets; `pivot` names the point that stays when only the size changes. `grid: "3x2"` + `cell: "1,0,2,1"` (0-based,
  spans optional) with `gap` and `margin`. `min_*` / `max_*` clamp the size; `fit: "move" | "shrink"` keeps the frame
  inside the area. A frame whose top strip leaves no grabbable piece on any work area is refused (`target_offscreen`)
  unless `allow_offscreen`.
- **Targets.** `window_id` (default `"active"`, the window frontmost when the request started), or `app` (exact,
  case-insensitive), `bundle_id` (macOS bundle id; Linux and Windows the window class), `title` (contains),
  `title_regex` (no look-around, backreferences, named groups; `(?i)` at the start ignores case), `pid`, combined with
  AND. Several matches: the frontmost (`on_multiple: "first"`, warning `multiple_matches:<n>`), `"error"`
  (`ambiguous_target`) or `"all"`; `nth` picks one. Front to back is the list order on Windows and the reversed list
  on the GNOME Shell and KWin backends (they list in stacking order, bottom first; probe P7 on GNOME); on X11 (the
  native module) and macOS it is not known, so the active window comes first and then the list's order, with the
  request warning `order_unreliable`. No match: `window_not_found`, or `skipped` with `if_missing: "skip"`; `wait_ms` waits for a
  window that is about to appear. A window claimed by one placement is not a candidate for a later one, so two
  placements with `app: "Terminal"` place two Terminal windows. SMBAct's own windows and black-listed apps are never
  matched (by id: `window_not_allowed`, `window_black_listed`).
- **State.** Maximized (also on one axis), minimized and fullscreen windows are brought back to normal first and then
  placed (`state_changes`: `unmaximized`, `unmaximized_vertical`, `unminimized`, `left_fullscreen`); after an
  un-minimize, which is an activation on Linux, the focus goes back to the window that was active at the start
  (warning `focus_denied` if the OS refuses). `state: "keep"` refuses such a window instead (`invalid_window_state`).
  A window on a desktop that is not showing: in place where the OS can, `window_on_other_desktop` on macOS
  (`desktop: "refuse"` refuses it everywhere; `desktop: "bring"` comes later).
- **Read-back.** After each write the window is read until two reads agree (at most 600 ms, macOS 800 ms). A row is
  `exact` when every component is within `tolerance` (default 1), else one corrective retry (the far edge of a right or
  bottom anchor, the centre and `fit` still hold) and then `adjusted` with `reasons`: `size_limited_min`,
  `size_limited_max`, `size_increment`, `not_resizable`, `position_limited`, `moved_by_app`, `no_effect` (no retry),
  `not_settled`, `unknown`. `strict` makes an adjusted row `failed` with `constraint`. A frame equal to the current one
  is `unchanged` and nothing is written (the round trip has no side effects).
- **Result.** `{status, coordinates, results, focus, warnings, ms}`. `status`: `applied`, `partial` (some rows failed),
  `failed`, `dry_run`. Each row: `placement`, `status` (`exact`, `adjusted`, `unchanged`, `would_place`, `skipped`,
  `failed`, `not_attempted`), `window` (`id`, `app`, `title`), `display`, `before` (before any state change),
  `requested`, `actual`, `delta`, `reasons`, `state_changes`, `warnings`, `attempts`, `ms`, `error`. A `failed` request
  is `isError` with the whole object plus the first failed row's `error` and `message` (today's error shape); a
  `partial` one is not an error: read the rows. A refusal before anything was resolved (`invalid_params`,
  `duplicate_target`, `license_required`, `busy`, `rate_limited`) has the plain error shape.
- **Dry run and simulation.** `dry_run: true` resolves everything and moves nothing (`would_place`, the state changes it
  would make, warning `state_dependent` for a window that is not normal). With `simulate: {displays, window?, os?}` it
  uses those displays and that frame instead of the real ones and looks up no window.
- **Order and limits.** Placements run one after another, best effort; `timeout_ms` (default 10000, at most 14000)
  covers the request, each placement at most 3 s (5 s leaving macOS fullscreen): a placement still running then fails
  with `timeout` and the rest are `not_attempted`. One request at a time: at most 4 wait (`busy`), at most 10 a second
  per entry point (`rate_limited`), at most 64 windows written. If the window engine restarts during a placement it
  waits up to 3 s and repeats that placement once (warning `engine_restarted`). A placement does not enter
  `window_action restore`'s history (Q12).
- **Not yet** (later phases): `focus`, `raise` and `atomic` (refused with `invalid_params` naming the phase),
  `smbact://place` links, saved scenes, `desktop: "bring"`, display hot-plug during a request.

The keys, from the manifest (`app-native/shared/placement/keys.ts`; `npm run catalog:gen` writes this table and
`placement.manifest.json`, which smbact-cli's flags are generated from; `npm run test:catalog` fails when either is
stale):

The key table is in `placement-keys.md`.
